name: Pause, Stop, Hide
explanation: Any content that moves, blinks, scrolls, or updates itself automatically — a carousel, a ticking news ticker, an auto-refreshing stock price — needs a way for the user to pause, stop, or hide it if it runs longer than five seconds and sits alongside other content. The user needs this control because moving content competing for attention next to text someone is trying to read makes that text much harder to focus on and process. The one exception is when the movement or update is essential to what the content actually is, like a video player showing a video.
whoItAffects: People with attention-related or cognitive disabilities can find it very difficult to read or concentrate on static content while something nearby is moving, flashing, or refreshing. People with low vision using screen magnification may lose track of moving content that shifts position while they're only viewing a portion of the screen at a time. Screen reader users can be interrupted mid-sentence when an auto-updating region announces new content over what they're currently listening to, if the update isn't handled carefully.

codeExample.bad:
Slide 1
Slide 2
Slide 3
codeExample.good:
Slide 1
Slide 2
Slide 3

howToTest: Look for anything on the page that moves, blinks, scrolls, or updates on its own without you interacting with it: carousels, marquees, auto-playing video previews, live-updating tickers or feeds. Time how long it runs — if it continues for more than five seconds and sits next to other content, check for a visible, keyboard-reachable control to pause, stop, or hide it. If no such control exists, and the movement isn't essential to the content itself, this fails.

check.question: A homepage has a promotional carousel that auto-advances every 4 seconds indefinitely, with no pause button and no way to stop it. Does this pass SC 2.2.2 Pause, Stop, Hide?
choices: Yes, because 4 seconds per slide is fast enough to not be distracting
No, because the carousel runs longer than five seconds total with no way to pause, stop, or hide it
Yes, because carousels are a standard, expected web pattern
It depends only on whether the carousel includes images or text
